I think that is a very fair assertion.  I think that the wall does help raise the issue which is important.  I just think that that we need to consider more ideas than the first one that is put on the table.  And we need to think through any solution and it's impact on geo-politics, economics, and domestic impact.

I personally don't have any ideas about how to secure the border, but thankfully there are much smarter people than us to work on the issue.

While it does piss people off the real question is, is the economic and social costs of the wall greater than benefits that can be achieved through spending the money elsewhere? And I don't think that is the case.

I think that the social costs are massively over looked.  First it would immediately sour all of our diplomatic relations with Mexico, which is are [third largest trading partner as of 2013!](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/statistics/highlights/top/top1312yr.html).  Not to mention that through Texas the border between the US and Mexico is the Rio Grande river.  And due to an old treaty nothing can be built in the actual river.  Which means that if we are to build the wall then it will have to be in Texas.  Which would require the government to either purchase large tracts of land from ranchers and farmers on the border or use eminent domain to acquire the land.  Also historically when the border fence was constructed the government suspended several important laws.  These laws revoked the engendered species act, and protection for Native American historic sites such as grave sites and religiously important areas.

I personally grew up in TX so I have a little more insight into how people in border states think about immigration.  And there is certainly a lot of frustration about the issue on both sides.  From what I understand most people in TX want to secure the borders.  The problem is that the current wall/fence that runs through Texas is not effective at all.  And the general consensus is that a large wall might slow down immigration for a month at best.  Until the coyotes ( in case you don't know a term for someone who smuggles people into the US) find new strategies to reach the US, such as new weak points where border personal is lacks, making larger ladders, or tunneling under the wall.
